newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower on blue chips selldown.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower on blue chips selldown.

text.p: * Decliners number almost five times more than gainers
Manila shares finished lower on Tuesday due to a selldown in selected big cap issues though some of the early losses were cut down by short-covering, traders said.
"The way we look at it, people were preparing for the initial public offering of Equitable," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital.
The main index closed 17.59 points down at 3,302.82 points.
The main index dipped by as much as 51.16 points, or 1.56 percent, to its intra-day low of 3,269.25.
There were 113 decliners against 23 gainers and 75 issues were unchanged.
Leading decliners among the blue chips were San Miguel B and Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co.
Volume of shares traded was at 22.645 billion valued at 3.397 billion pesos.
Traders said the market ignored positive economic news such as higher export figures announced by the government shortly before trading started.
"There was short-covering as some people who sold at the beginning bought back at close," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities.
The market on Wednesday may be brightened by PLDT's announcement of a 100 percent stock dividend, traders said.
The Philippine Stock Exchange halted trading of the stock prior to the close of session on PLDT's advisory.

The PSE surveillance department said it had to stop trading of the index heavyweight until the disclosure was disseminated to all its member brokers. The PSE said trading of PLDT will resume on Wednesday.

Aside from news on PLDT, the initial public offering of Equitable Banking Corp and expectations of lower inflation figures for February would likely spur investors to venture into the market, brokers said.
